subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw core accept per-agent managed plugin installs now, and what is the canonical contract for record identity, discovery precedence, update/uninstall cleanup, and security isolation?
rationale: The PR changes public plugin CLI behavior and persisted plugin state in a security-sensitive lifecycle area, and the linked issue is still explicitly marked for product and security review.

options.title: Pause for contract first
options.body: Keep the PR open but require a maintainer-owned contract and a revised implementation that updates install, uninstall, update, inspect, discovery, docs, and proof together.

options.title: Narrow to install-record groundwork
options.body: Ask the contributor to remove public CLI exposure and land only internal preparatory pieces after they no longer change user-visible behavior.

options.title: Close in favor of the canonical issue
options.body: If maintainers do not want this branch as the landing path, close it and continue design in the linked feature issue.

recommendation.title: Pause for contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require a maintainer-owned contract and a revised implementation that updates install, uninstall, update, inspect, discovery, docs, and proof together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is prior ownership of the installed plugin index and managed npm install isolation work that this feature must extend.
